inputs. ::: {.fragment} `dplyr` style: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} pdxTrees %>% rename(ht = Tree_Height, pol = Pollution_Removal_oz) %>% summarize(across(.cols = c(DBH, ht, store the anonymous function. * Also called lambda function/expression. ::: ::: {.fragment} Longform syntax: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} pdxTrees %>% rename(ht = Tree_Height, Loops **Language**: Iterating = Looping ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # Data pdxTrees <- get_pdxTrees_parks() # Variables of interest vars <- c("DBH", "Tree_Height", "Pollution_Removal_oz") # Vector for storing output pdxTrees_coef_of_vars <- rep(NA, 3) # For loop for(i in 1:3){ pdxTrees_coef_of_vars[i] <- coef_of_var(pdxTrees[[vars[i]]], na.rm = TRUE) } # Examine `for()` Loop Components ::: {.nonincremental} * **Output**: What you want to produce and store. + Good to specify size of output object. + Start with `NA`s so clear which have been replaced. + vector("double", 3) pdxTrees_coef_of_vars ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0 0 0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} pdxTrees_coef_of_vars <- vector() pdxTrees_coef_of_vars ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` logical(0) ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} pdxTrees_coef_of_vars <- rep(NA, 3) pdxTrees_coef_of_vars ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] NA NA NA ``` ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### `for()` Loop Components **Sequence**: The vector you want to iterate over ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # Sequence Options 1:3 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1 2 3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} 1:length(pdxTrees_coef_of_vars) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1 2 3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} seq_along(pdxTrees_coef_of_vars) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1 2 3 ``` ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### `for()` Loop Components **Body**: The code that we iterate. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} for(i in seq_along(pdxTrees_coef_of_vars)){ pdxTrees_coef_of_vars[i] <- coef_of_var(pdxTrees[[vars[i]]], na.rm = TRUE) } pdxTrees_coef_of_vars ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.6496634 0.6129159 0.8835582 ``` ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Another example: Building Up a `for()` Loop I want to construct a bootstrap distribution for the mean `DBH` for our sample of Portland trees. * How is looping/iterating helpful here? ::: {.fragment .nonincremental} * Let's start with a minimal viable product. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} mean(sample(pdxTrees$DBH, replace = TRUE)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 20.66442 ``` ::: ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Another example: Building Up a `for()` Loop * What do I want to store? + What type of R object do I want? + What's the required size? ::: {.fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} boot <- data.frame(avg = rep(NA, 1000)) ``` ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Another example: Building Up a `for()` Loop How do I save this in `boot`? ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} mean(sample(pdxTrees$DBH, replace = TRUE)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 20.49086 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # Set i for now i <- 1 # Option 1 boot[i, ] <- mean(sample(pdxTrees$DBH, replace = TRUE)) boot[i, ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 20.57264 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Option 2 boot$avg[i] <- mean(sample(pdxTrees$DBH, replace = TRUE)) boot$avg[i] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 20.65612 ``` ::: ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Another example: Building Up a `for()` Loop ::: {.cell layout-align="center" output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} boot <- data.frame(avg = rep(NA, 1000)) for(i in seq_along(boot$avg)){ boot[i,] <- mean(sample(pdxTrees$DBH, replace = TRUE)) } ggplot(data = boot, mapping = aes(x = avg)) + geom_density() ``` ::: We can also **nest** loops: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} boot <- data.frame(avg_n_20 = rep(NA, 1000), avg_n_50 = rep(NA, 1000), avg_n_100 = rep(NA, 1000)) sizes <- c(20, 50, 100) for(j in 1:ncol(boot)){ # Generate sample samp <- sample(pdxTrees$DBH, size = sizes[j]) for(i in 1:nrow(boot)){ boot[i,j] <- mean(sample(samp, replace = TRUE)) } } glimpse(boot) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center" output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} boot %>% pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "n", values_to = "avg") %>% mutate(n = parse_number(n)) %>% ggplot(aes(x = avg)) + geom_density() + facet_wrap(~n, ncol = 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](math241_wk10mon_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-21-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Need an Unknown Number of Iterations * If you want to iterate `while` some condition is true, then you don't necessarily know how many iterations are required beforehand. * Will then use a `while()` loop instead of a `for()` loop. ::: {.fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} for(i in 1:???){ # Do Something } while(condition) { # Do Something } ``` ::: ::: * Keeps iterating as long as the condition holds. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### `while()` Loop Example Want 20 random draws from a normal that are positive numbers ::: {.fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} norm_pos <- vector() i <- 0 while(length(norm_pos) < 20){ # Random draw draw <- rnorm(n = 1) # Only add positive draws if(draw > 0){ norm_pos <- c(norm_pos, draw) } } glimpse(norm_pos) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` num [1:20] 0.3184 0.991 0.0783 0.3249 0.6261 ... ``` ::: ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Loops * `while()` loops aren't nearly as common as `for()` loops. * For those who go into statistics research, you will end up often using `for()` loops to run simulation studies. ::: {.fragment .nonincremental} * The internet hates `for()` loops in R. + But they usually aren't as slow as people say. ::: ::: {.fragment .nonincremental} * Alternatives: + `apply()` functions + `purrr` functions ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(purrr) ``` ::: ::: # Function Programming with `purrr` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](img/purrr.png){fig-align='center' width=20%} ::: ::: {.fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} pdxTrees %>% select(DBH, Tree_Height, Pollution_Removal_oz) %>% map(.f = mean, na.rm = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### `map_XXX` Functions :::: {.columns} ::: {.column .nonincremental} * Loop over an R object * Do something * Save results ::: ::: {.column .nonincremental .fragment} * Function for each type of output: + `map()` makes a list. + `map_lgl()` makes a logical vector. + `map_int()` makes an integer vector. + `map_dbl()` makes a double vector. + `map_chr()` makes a character vector. + `map_df()` makes a data frame. ::: :::: ::: {.fragment} General structure: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} map_XXX(.x, .f, ...) ``` ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### `map_XXX` Functions ::: {.nonincremental} * Input: vector + What did `map_XXX()` iterate over? ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- c(1, 3, 6, 2) map_lgl(x, .f = ~(.x > 5 )) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE FALSE TRUE FALSE ``` ::: :::
